picks.summary:
The Less You Seek, The More You’ll Find | The Happiness Paradox
Taoism for Inner Peace (book): https://einzelganger.co/tao/The less we try to think about a blue elephant, the more likely this creature persists in residing in our thoughts. Imagine the blue elephant represents our unhappiness - our dissatisfaction with life - hence the color blue. Obviously, no one likes feeling blue, and when we experience it, we’re likely to try getting rid of it. picks.reason: Considers Taoist ideas on desire, happiness, and acceptance of suffering.

picks.title: Ep. 106 - An Interview with Zen teacher Mitra Bishop (Zen Podcast)
picks.summary: Our guest in this episode is Mitra Bishop Roshi. She received a B.A. from Indiana University, raised two children, and worked in graphic, interior, and architectural design for many years. She first encountered Buddhism while living in Asia. She was ordained at the Rochester Zen Center, where she lived and practiced for many years and received dharma transmission from Kapleau Roshi. Afterwards she traveled to Sogen-ji in Japan to practice under the guidance of the Zen master, Harada Shodo Roshi. She currently lives in New Mexico, where she has founded Mountain Gate. For more information about
picks.reason: A Zen teacher discusses Buddhist practice and insight into mind and life.

picks.showTitle: The Road Home with Ethan Nichtern
picks.title: Ep 182 - The Three Poisons
picks.summary: On the latest episode of The Road Home podcast, we dive into one of the deepest and most crucial teachings of Buddhist philosophy of the mind: the three poisons. These could also be called the three confused habitual responses to the present moment. In this dharma talk, we go "under the hood" of how our moment by moment experience unfolds, and how our observation of our confusion can be simplified to the exploration of three simple momentary experiences, as well as our three confused reactions to them.
